Implementation Plan

Planning ref: `claude/heal-evidence-bundle` @ `947c9099653617917889c6859ca4b0dcfce90a05` (matches the integration branch metadata; no mismatch).

Scope-mode: Selective Expansion
Reuse-audit: extends has_config_hazard
Scope-mode justification: The finding is a gap in the existing fail-closed check in `scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh`. The `hazard_re` deny-list at line 29 covers credential, proxy, URL-rewrite and include keys, but it misses every config key that makes Git run a program. So a `filter.<x>.clean` driver in `.git/config`, switched on by `.git/info/attributes`, passes `restore` and later runs with the PAT back in the checkout. The core fix extends `hazard_re` and `has_config_hazard`. Two more pieces are added in the same PR, each under 30 LOC with no new dependency or external interface: (1) an attributes-file check, and (2) a `check` action that `scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh` calls before its first git command, which closes the time gap between `restore` and `git add`. Under the boil-the-lake rule they belong here. They are ordered by the core priorities in `unattended_system_instructions.md` §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), and completeness improves correctness. Out of scope: narrowing the GH_PAT itself (an operator/secret change) and blocking editor-written `.git/hooks` (see D3).

## Automation / wiring (§20.E)
- Change type: modifies existing code only. It extends `scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh` (adds a `check` action next to `hide|restore`) and adds one call in `scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh`. No new script.
- Scheduler / PR-push entry point: none new. It runs inside the existing `.github/workflows/implement.yml` job (issue-comment `/approved` trigger):
  - the existing `hide`/`restore` calls at lines ~2717, 2865, 2883, 4136, 4153, 4159 and 4252;
  - the existing "Commit changes" step (line ~4346), which runs `implement_commit_changes.sh`.
  - `editor_git_credentials.sh` is already staged into `IMPLEMENT_STAGED_SUPPORT_RUN_DIR` (implement.yml line 1027) and into plan.yml (line 286). No workflow YAML edits are needed, and `implement.yml` (324,275 bytes) stays the same size.
- Long-running supervisor: not required.
- DB work: none.
- `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`: no entry, because no new script is added.

## Files likely to change
1. `scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh`
   - Extend `hazard_re` (line 29) with keys that make Git run a program (lowercase, like the existing regex):
     - `filter\..*\.(clean|smudge|process)`
     - `diff\.external`, `diff\..*\.(command|textconv)`
     - `merge\..*\.driver`
     - `core\.attributesfile`
     - `core\.alternaterefscommand`
     - `gpg\.(.*\.)?program`
     - `remote\..*\.(uploadpack|receivepack)`
     - `uploadpack\.packobjectshook`
     - `lfs\..*` (to block `lfs.customtransfer.*.path` and similar)
   - The existing rule stays: only `system` and `command` scopes are trusted, so the runner's system-scope `filter.lfs.*` (checked on this runner) still passes. Update the comment above `hazard_re` to say it now also covers keys that run commands.
   - Add `has_attributes_hazard()`. It returns true (hazard) when either file exists and has a non-comment line assigning `filter=`, `diff=` or `merge=`:
     - the checkout's `$(repo_git "$repo" rev-parse --git-path info/attributes)`, resolved against the repo when relative;
     - the global default attributes file `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/git/attributes`.
     - It also returns true when either file is unreadable or a symlink (fail closed).
     - Tracked in-tree `.gitattributes` is repository content and is not checked. Any driver it names is harmless once the config check above holds (D2).
   - Call `has_attributes_hazard` next to `has_config_hazard` in `hide` (line ~157) and `restore` (line ~283), logging the new reason `attributes_hazard`.
   - Add action `check`:
     - Update the usage `case` at line 21 to `hide|restore|check`.
     - Run it before the marker logic. It needs no marker, no token and no `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`.
     - For each repo in `repos` that `is_checkout_root` accepts, run `has_config_hazard` and `has_attributes_hazard`.
     - Also run one config-hazard lookup in the caller's own environment, so an exported `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` (implement exports them) is checked as the config the following `git add` will actually read. Do this by adding a variant without `env -u`, e.g. a `has_config_hazard_effective` that runs `git config --show-scope --get-regexp` with the inherited environment.
     - Exit 1 on any hazard, logging `EDITOR_GIT_CREDENTIALS action=check repo=<label> removed=none outcome=refused reason=config_hazard|attributes_hazard`. Exit 0 otherwise.
   - Update the header comment and the exit-code doc.
2. `scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh`
   - At the top, before the first git invocation (ahead of the staged-support ledger handling and the `git add -u` at line 344), add:
     `bash "${IMPLEMENT_STAGED_SUPPORT_RUN_DIR:-scripts}/editor_git_credentials.sh" check || { echo "::error::Editor-writable git config or attributes would run a command during staging; refusing to commit."; exit 1; }`
   - If the helper file is missing, fail closed with the same `::error::`, because the helper is always staged.
   - Also pass `-c core.fsmonitor=false` on the two `git add` invocations (lines 344–345) as defense in depth. Command scope overrides local config. Existing code already uses `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null` on commit.
3. `tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py` — new tests (see Testing).
4. `agents.md` — in the "Implement self-repo staged-support ledger" bullet that describes `scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh`, add command-running driver keys (filter/diff/merge drivers, `core.attributesFile`, gpg program, `lfs.*`), driver lines in `info/attributes` / global attributes, and the new `check` call before staging. The log prefix `EDITOR_GIT_CREDENTIALS` is unchanged.
5. `changelog.d/6456-editor-git-filter-hazard.md` — new fragment following CLAUDE.md §20, with a Security entry.

## Functions / modules
- `hazard_re`: extended. Same variable, no rename.
- `has_config_hazard`: unchanged logic; the regex widens.
- New `has_attributes_hazard <repo>`. Name checked: not present in the file.
- New `has_config_hazard_effective` (inherited-env lookup). Name checked: not present.
- New `check` branch in the action dispatch.
- `implement_commit_changes.sh`: one guarded call at the top, plus `-c core.fsmonitor=false` on `git add`.

## Data structures affected
- Marker file format: unchanged.
- No state, JSON or label changes. New log reason values `attributes_hazard` and `action=check` are added alongside the existing ones.

## API / interface changes
- `editor_git_credentials.sh` gains `check [repo...]`. Exit codes: 0 clean, 1 refused, 2 usage. `hide`/`restore` keep their behavior except for the extra refusals.
- No new env vars, so §8 defaults are not affected.

Data flow:
1. hide: validate config + attributes → strip token.
2. Editor runs (untrusted; can write `.git/config`, `.git/info/attributes`, `~/.gitconfig`, `~/.config/git/attributes`).
3. restore: validate origin + config hazards (now including drivers) + attributes. Any failure → refuse; no token is injected.
4. The commit step calls `check`, which re-validates right before `git add` (closes the gap for editor processes that outlive the editor).
5. `git add` (fsmonitor forced off) → scope guard → `commit -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null` → push.

Failure modes:
- Editor plants a filter driver plus `info/attributes`. Symptom: `restore` exits 1 with `reason=config_hazard` (or `attributes_hazard`); the implement step fails and no token is written. Recovery: the existing failure path; a re-issued implement runs on a fresh runner.
- A background process re-plants config after `restore`. Symptom: the "Commit changes" step exits 1 with `action=check ... outcome=refused`. Recovery: same as above.
- Legitimate local LFS filter config (a checkout with `lfs: true` runs `git lfs install --local`). Symptom: `hide` refuses with `config_hazard`. Today implement.yml has no `lfs:` input (checked with grep), so nothing is affected now. Recovery if that ever changes: pin the canonical git-lfs values (D1 alternative).
- A runner image with filter config in global rather than system scope. Symptom: `hide` refuses before the editor runs. On this runner it is in system scope; noted as a risk.

## Decisions
### D1 — Refuse command-running driver keys in editor-writable scopes
- Chosen: extend the existing `hazard_re` scope rule (only system/command scopes are trusted) to filter, diff, merge, gpg, attributesFile, alternateRefsCommand, upload/receive-pack and `lfs.*` keys.
- Alternatives considered: snapshot all config at `hide` and compare at `restore` (rejected: the marker lives in an editor-writable directory, so the snapshot could be forged); allow-list exact git-lfs values in local scope (not needed: LFS is configured at system scope and implement checkouts do not enable LFS).
- Why: it matches the existing fail-closed design, needs no extra trust anchor, and blocks the reported exploit at its root (driver definition) whatever activates it.

### D2 — Check only git-internal and global attribute files, not tracked `.gitattributes`
- Chosen: refuse driver assignments in `info/attributes` and the global default attributes file.
- Alternatives considered: check tracked `.gitattributes` too (rejected: legitimate repo content such as `filter=lfs` would fail runs); skip attribute checks entirely (rejected: the finding asks for it, and it costs little).
- Why: once D1 holds, attributes cannot run anything by themselves; this is a cheap second layer aimed at the exploit's activation step.

### D3 — Do not refuse `core.hooksPath` or editor-written hooks
- Chosen: leave hooks to the existing `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/nul
